title: Subsets
description: Generate all subsets of a set using the include/exclude backtracking pattern.

data.text: Given an integer array `nums` of unique elements, return all possible subsets (the power set). The solution set must not contain duplicate subsets; return them in any order.

At each index, branch twice: once including `nums[i]` in the current subset and once excluding it. When the index passes the last element, record a copy of the current subset. There are `n` decisions of two choices each, giving `2^n` subsets and `O(n)` depth.

data.title: Include/Exclude O(2^n)

data.text: The same idea expressed as the canonical backtracking template: record the current subset, then loop from the current index, choosing each remaining element in turn and recursing. This generalizes directly to combinations and permutations.

data.title: Backtracking template

data.caption: The include/exclude decision tree for [1,2,3]. Every node is a subset; leaves are the fully-decided subsets.
data.definition:
graph TB
    A[[]] --> B[include 1]
    A --> C[exclude 1]
    B --> D[[1]]
    D --> E[[1,2]]
    E --> F[[1,2,3]]
    C --> G[[2]]
    G --> H[[2,3]]
    C --> I[[3]]
    style F fill:#e8f5e9,stroke:#2e7d32

data.title: What improved?
data.text: Both are O(2^n) in the number of subsets — that's inherent, since the output itself has 2^n subsets. The backtracking template matters because the *same* structure solves combinations, permutations, and combination-sum: only the loop bounds and pruning change.
